narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Site Handover Log" (Sổ giao ca công trường)**

A handover log is read at the start of a shift: it says what is waiting, which project it belongs to, who has it and what happens next. Every Nicon admin screen answers the same four questions before anything else: **Where am I? What is waiting for me? What can I do next? Did it work?**

Staff are nontechnical construction people working in Vietnamese first. The screens are bright, flat and legible: white working surfaces on a quiet backdrop, thin rules, Nicon red reserved for the next main action, and a small shared set of status colours that always carry words. Records that need action stand out; finished records stay quiet.

The voice is clear and friendly. Sentences are short, use construction and Nicon business words, and say what happened and what to do next. No technical jargon, error codes or internal names appear in ordinary screens.

This standard covers authenticated admin screens. The public website has its own visual language and does not lend it to the workspace. `AGENTS.md` and the business contracts take precedence over visual choices. This file is the standard to apply; it does not claim that every screen already meets it.
keyCharacteristics: One project context and one page title; related panels share the frame.
Waiting and blocked work is more visible than finished work.
The reason for a state sits beside the action that resolves it.
Motion confirms what the user just did, and stops when they ask for less.
Loading, empty, error, success and no-permission states look different.
BCH works well on a phone; CM supports desktop comparison and the keyboard.

rules.name: The One Red Voice Rule
rules.body: Each working area has at most one filled red action. Everything else is outline or ghost.

rules.name: The Words First Rule
rules.body: Remove all colour and every status must still be understood from its label.

rules.name: The Same Word, Same Tone Rule
rules.body: A lifecycle meaning maps to one tone across modules. Do not assign a colour by matching an English status name; decide what the state means in its own lifecycle. A confirmed HSE violation is still open (warning), not a success.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase eyebrows, wide tracking or tiny chips as a second heading system. Existing uppercase utilities are legacy.

rules.name: The Never Broken Word Rule
rules.body: Names, codes and reasons wrap at spaces or hyphens. A column too narrow for that is the defect: merge reference data into one metadata line or switch to stacked cards.

rules.name: The Flat Work Surface Rule
rules.body: Records, forms and tables stay flat: border and tone, no glow or blur. Gradient and a soft shadow belong only to `StatTile`, the page icon and the attention counts; a stat tile that opens a list may lift 2px on hover. The translucent sticky top bar is the only blur.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: Express subsections with headings, rows and separators.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, movement, zoom and smooth scrolling stop and changes happen at once. This is one global rule, not something each screen remembers. A busy spinner may keep turning.

dos: **Do** show project, record, state and next permitted action together.
**Do** put waiting, overdue and blocked work where the eye lands first.
**Do** explain a blocked action: the reason and the step that unblocks it.
**Do** say what is true: a file waiting for Google Drive is not synchronized, a lost file is not "synced", missing actual progress is not 0%, a draft plan is not a published baseline.
**Do** keep typed input and decision reasons until the server confirms success.
**Do** write short, friendly Vietnamese first, with keys in all four languages.
**Do** check real content at 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px, at 200% zoom, with the keyboard, and with reduced motion on.

**Do** follow the server's authorization, independent-review and deletion-impact contracts: permanent deletion shows impact, blockers and file consequences and asks for the record code (`AGENTS.md`, Hard-delete policy).
donts: **Don't** hard-code status colours or use raw palette classes.
**Don't** use colour alone, or a tooltip or truncation alone, to carry a name, reason or prerequisite.
**Don't** make a row-level delete the loudest thing in a row.
**Don't** replace business names with internal IDs, abbreviations or raw JSON.
**Don't** invent records, formulas or counts to fill a dashboard, or call a list or chart complete when data is missing or truncated.
**Don't** close a dialog after a failed action or reset the user's work.
**Don't** put gradients on records, forms, buttons or table rows, and don't add glow, nested cards or entrance animation to work screens.
